title: Safety precautions: the revolver
subtitle: Making the revolver safe, the safety catch, and the magazine safety

lines: This episode covers making the revolver safe, the safety catch, and the magazine safety.
And we finish with how to be muzzle conscious.

scenes.caption: Making the revolver safe: steps 1 and 2
lines: Making the revolver safe starts just like the pistol.
Step one. Identify a safe direction.
Step two. Point the firearm in a safe direction, with your finger off the trigger.

scenes.caption: Steps 3 and 4: grip, then open the cylinder
lines: Step three. Place your left hand under the trigger guard, and your right thumb on the cylinder release catch.
Keep your trigger finger off the trigger.
Step four. Open the cylinder.
Make sure that your middle two fingers are on the cylinder and through the frame of the revolver.
Your middle two fingers and thumb now have control of the cylinder.

lines.text: Here are those parts on our revolver.
Your left hand goes under the trigger guard.
Your right thumb goes on the cylinder release catch.
Step five. Remove the ammunition from the cylinder by depressing the ejector rod.

scenes.caption: Step 5: depress the ejector rod
lines: In the book's photo, the ejector rod is depressed to push the ammunition out of the cylinder.
For the revolver, once the cylinder is open and the ammunition removed, no further steps are required.
And if you are handing over a revolver, the cylinder should be left open during the exchange.

scenes.heading: Safety catch
bullets: Others lock the slide, hammer and trigger
Hammer-drop safety catches lower the hammer
Engage: up on some, down or forwards on others
Red dot: on for some, off for others
lines: Next, the safety catch.
Safety catches work differently from one firearm to the next.

lines.text: Some safety catches will lock the trigger only.
Others will lock the slide, the hammer and the trigger.
Some will lower the hammer for you.

lines: These are known as hammer-drop safety catches.

lines.text: On some firearms you press the safety catch up to engage it, and on others down or forwards.
Some expose a red dot when the safety catch is on, while others may expose a red dot when it is off.

lines: These differences are because firearms come from different countries, with designs influenced by different cultures and languages.

scenes.heading: Know your safety catch

lines.text: Make sure that you are familiar with how the safety catch works on your particular firearm.

lines: Always remember, the safety catch is a mechanical device that can fail.
It is simply an additional safety precaution, and it must never replace your safety rules.

scenes.definition: Prevents the gun from being fired once the magazine has been removed.
lines: Some firearms are equipped with a magazine safety.
The magazine safety prevents the gun from being fired once the magazine has been removed.
Its purpose is to prevent an accidental discharge if someone removes the magazine and forgets to remove the round from the chamber.
Examples of firearms manufactured with a magazine safety are the Browning High Power and the Star Model B series.

lines.text: But they forget to remove the round from the chamber.
With a magazine safety, the gun cannot be fired once the magazine has been removed.

scenes.caption: Be Muzzle Conscious
lines: Finally, be muzzle conscious.
Notice the person holding the firearm is not aware that his firearm is pointing at innocent bystanders.
A competent firearm handler knows where his firearm is pointing at all times.
That is to say, you should at all times be aware of where the muzzle of your firearm is pointing.

scenes.question: What is a magazine safety?
options: It prevents firing once the magazine is removed
It lowers the hammer for you
lines: The exam asks this one.
What is a magazine safety?
reveal: The magazine safety prevents the gun from being fired once the magazine has been removed.
Lowering the hammer is what a hammer-drop safety catch does.

scenes.question: How do you remove the ammunition from the revolver?
options: Open the cylinder and depress the ejector rod
lines: How do you remove the ammunition when making a revolver safe?
reveal: Open the cylinder, then remove the ammunition from the cylinder by depressing the ejector rod.

points: Safe direction, finger off the trigger
Thumb on the cylinder release catch, open it
Magazine safety: no firing with magazine out
lines: So, identify a safe direction and point the revolver there, finger off the trigger.
Thumb on the cylinder release catch, and open the cylinder.
Remove the ammunition by depressing the ejector rod.
The safety catch can fail, and it never replaces your safety rules.
A magazine safety prevents firing once the magazine is removed.
And always be aware of where your muzzle is pointing.
